simple.meaning: גֶּרֶם (gerem) is a Hebrew word meaning “a bone (as the skeleton of the body); hence, self , i.e. (figuratively) very.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: גֶּרֶם (H1634) appears 5 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Genesis 49:14, with occurrences in Genesis, 2 Kings, Job, Proverbs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to גֶּרֶם (H1634) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in גֶּרֶם (H1634) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: גֶּרֶם (gerem) / H1634 is traced through Genesis 49:14, 2 Kings 9:13, Job 40:18, Proverbs 17:22 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H1634. gerem גֶּ֫רֶם noun [masculine] bone, strength, self (?) (Arabic body , Aramaic גְּרַם , bone, self ) — absolute גָּ֑רֶם Gen 49:14 2 t.; construct גֶּרֶם 2Kin 9:13 ; suffix גְּרָמָיו Job 40:18 ; 1 bone Prov 17:22 (collective) 25:15 ; of behemoth (hippopotamus) Job 40:18 (|| עצם q. v.) 2 strength Gen 49:14 גָּ֑רֶם חֲמֹר strong ass (literally bony , so VB). 3 self (compare עצם ), 2Kin 9:13 הַמַּעֲלוֺת גֶּרֶם so Ges Ew Ke, but text dubious, see conjectures in Klo. [ גְּרַם ] noun [masculine] bone (Biblical Hebrew גֶּ֫רֶם ; Christian-Palestinian Aramaic Schulth Lex. 46 ); — plural suffix גַּרְמֵיהוֺן Dan 6:25 .
